The drivers say which instruments are shut and which are live. Mixing bases on one ticker is unavoidable
on a Sunday evening; what is avoidable is doing it silently, so the "updated" strings differ accordingly.

WHY MONDAY MATTERS MORE THAN USUAL: Brent settled on Friday before almost everything that has happened
since. Since that settle there have been two further strikes on Riyadh airport, a US jet disabling a
cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman, about 69% of US Gulf of Mexico output still shut after Hurricane Isaias,
a suspension of US sanctions on Russian diesel, and a presidential claim that Ukraine and Russia have
agreed an energy ceasefire. Those pull in opposite directions and none of them is in the price yet.

GILT: unchanged from Friday's published 5.44. The three-way spread recorded on Friday — CNBC 5.4226 after
the cash close, Trading Economics 5.45, our own live read 5.4396 — is still unresolved and will only
settle on Monday's open.
